subject: ventures/worker-classification-checker
professional: an employment-tax and wage-and-hour practitioner (a CPA with payroll-tax controversy experience, or an employment lawyer doing worker-classification intake), who checks first that the Section 3509 rates and FLSA look-backs are right, that the tests are described as the IRS/DOL/state agencies apply them, and that state-by-state differences are not flattened

evidence.correctness: Ran node --test calc.test.mjs page.test.mjs usage.test.mjs: 32 pass, 0 fail. Recomputed exposure() independently in a separate Python script from IRC 3509(a)/(b), FICA 7.65%, FUTA 0.6% on $7,000 and FLSA 29 USC 216(b)/255(a) (2 yr, 3 willful; liquidated = equal amount): (1) $60,000, 50 h/wk, 2 yr, 1099s filed: tax rate 0.0765+0.015+0.2*0.0765=10.68% -> 12,816; FUTA 84; OT premium 10 h * 0.5 * $23.0769 * 52 * 2 = 12,000; full FICA 15.3% = 18,360; low 24,900, high 42,444; tool output identical. (2) $60,000, 40 h, 1 yr, 3 workers, no 1099s: rate 13.71% -> 24,678; FUTA 126; high 27,666; identical. (3) $5,000, 45 h, 3 yr willful: payroll 1,602, FUTA 90 (min(pay,7000)), OT 833.33 over 3 yr, high 4,051.67; identical. Also checked 5 years non-willful caps at 2 look-back years, and bad inputs (hours 0, non-numeric pay) return an error object, not NaN. The arithmetic matches the statute. Limits: FUTA at 0.6% assumes the full 5.4% state credit, the high case omits income-tax withholding liability, and neither is stated on the page; the Social Security wage base is disclosed as ignored. Classification scores were checked by hand for the 3-question case in the tests and for a 'contractor with only core_work=yes' case (IRS share 9.1% contractor, ABC employee), which behaves as documented. Not capped by reading only: it ran.
evidence.completeness: Checked each README/page feature by running it: 16 questions with a select each (page.test confirms generation from QUESTIONS); IRS and DOL weighted-share verdicts (60% / 35% thresholds as README states); ABC by prong with burden on the hirer (unsure = not shown) works; 'what to change' list (topFlags) works; exposure range with §3509 filed/unfiled rates, FUTA, overtime premium, 2/3 year look-back, liquidated damages works; example loader and reset wired; privacy/usage opt-out present. 'What this does not cover' list on the README matches the page. No stubs or TODOs found. Not built (and not claimed): saved per-worker audit file / printable memo, which VENTURE.yaml lists as a not-built paid tier. The overall `risk` field from evaluate() is computed and tested but never shown on the page (dead output).
evidence.verification: node --test calc.test.mjs page.test.mjs usage.test.mjs: 32 tests, 32 pass. Seeded four mutations in calc.mjs, one at a time, ran calc.test.mjs, reverted with git checkout (git status clean afterwards). (a) abc_c cluster threshold share < 0.5 -> < 0.6: 16/16 pass, NOT caught. (b) IRS/DOL employee verdict threshold share >= 0.6 -> >= 0.7: 16/16 pass, NOT caught. (c) willful look-back 3 -> 3 in both branches (drop the 2-year non-willful limit): caught (1 fail). (d) filed-case s3509 employee-FICA share 0.2 -> 0.25: caught (1 fail). So the money arithmetic is well pinned, but the classification boundaries, which are the product's headline output, are only tested at the extremes (all-employee, all-contractor, one weak fact), so two of four mutants survive. Page tests are regex checks on the HTML source; nothing renders the page or executes the inline script.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (all), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, usage.mjs, index.html script and head. Pure functions, no dependencies, input validation returns an error object, HTML output escaped with esc(), questions are data with weights. Defects: rate constants and weights are unexplained magic numbers (no citation next to each weight); `link rel=canonical href=./index.html`, `sitemap.xml <loc>./index.html</loc>` and the robots.txt `Sitemap: ./sitemap.xml` use relative URLs that crawlers ignore or reject; `risk` is computed but unused; the `high` bound uses min/max sorting to hide any case where low > high instead of modelling it. Nothing silent-failing in the maths.
evidence.claims: Disclaimer present and strong on the page ('No warranty ... not legal, tax, or financial advice', FAQ 'Is this legal advice?', explicit skipped-items list incl. VCSP, Section 530, wage base, AB 5), asserted by page.test.mjs; README says 'A screening aid, not legal advice'. Checked claims: 'sixteen yes/no questions' -> 16 questions in QUESTIONS (but the selects are Yes/No/Not sure, so 'yes/no' is a slight simplification); 'nothing is uploaded / entirely client-side' -> index.html loads only ./calc.mjs and ./usage.mjs, no fetch of user answers (usage.mjs records counters; opt-out exists); 'Section 3509 1.5%/20%, 3%/40%' -> matches IRC 3509(a),(b) and RATES; 'FUTA on first $7,000' -> matches; 'half-time overtime premium, 2 yr (3 willful)' -> matches the FLSA. Weaknesses: README says ABC applies to 'wage, unemployment and payroll law in states such as CA, MA, NJ and IL', but Illinois' ABC prong test is for unemployment insurance only, and the page does not tell the user the ABC result only matters in states that apply it; llms.txt links the old duncan-haywood.github.io address rather than the live marisstella.app URL; the README 'After using this ...' sentence 'used to take a lawyer's intake call' is promotional but harmless. No fake reviews or numbers.
evidence.fitness: Walked a small-business owner with one full-time 1099 bookkeeper: answers 16 questions, gets three verdicts, a ranked list of facts to change, and a dollar range, in a few minutes with no signup; that is a real first screen. Gaps the owner hits in the first hour: no way to say which state they are in, so the ABC verdict (which is binding only in some states) is shown as one of three co-equal results and can read 'employee' for a worker who passes the IRS and DOL tests in a non-ABC state; no way to save or print a result for counsel (not built); overtime exposure assumes the worker is non-exempt, but a salaried misclassified worker paid above the salary threshold with exempt duties would owe no overtime, and that is not mentioned; exposure uses a single pay figure and cannot be broken down by year or worker. It does not replace a lawyer but, honestly labelled, does the screening job.
evidence.domain: Compared against the IRS three-category common-law framework (behavioral control, financial control, type of relationship, Rev. Rul. 87-41 / Pub. 15-A), the DOL FLSA economic reality factors (opportunity for profit or loss, investment, permanence, control, integral work, skill and initiative; 29 CFR 795), and the ABC prongs of Dynamex/AB 5 (Cal. Lab. Code 2775), Mass. G.L. c.149 s.148B and NJ. The factor taxonomy and the burden-on-hirer treatment of ABC are sound and the hirer-unfavourable handling of 'unsure' is what a practitioner would want. Departures: weights and the 60%/35% cutoffs are the author's heuristic and are not claimed to come from any authority, yet are presented as a percentage 'weight of the facts'; IRS and DOL are treated as additive scoring though courts and the IRS explicitly refuse mechanical counting; state ABC variants differ (NJ and IL prong B add a 'places of business' alternative, MA prong B is narrower) and are flattened into one rule; the DOL rule's current enforcement status is not mentioned; exposure ignores the Section 530 safe harbor in the number (only mentioned as skipped), income-tax withholding at full rate in the high case, the §3509(c) bar, FUTA credit assumptions and overtime exemption. A practitioner would accept it as an intake checklist, not as an exposure estimator.

defects.what: Classification thresholds are untested: raising the employee-verdict cutoff 0.6->0.7 and the ABC prong C cutoff 0.5->0.6 both leave all 16 calc tests passing.

ABC verdict is shown alongside IRS and DOL as an equal result with no state selector or note that it only binds in states that apply it (and not for IL wage law); an owner outside those states sees 'Leans employee' from a test that does not govern them.

Exposure assumes overtime is owed for every hour above 40 (non-exempt) and a 5.4% FUTA state credit, and the high case omits income-tax withholding liability; none of these assumptions is stated beside the number.
canonical link, sitemap loc and robots Sitemap line are relative URLs, which search engines do not accept; llms.txt links the superseded duncan-haywood.github.io address instead of marisstella.app.
evaluate().risk is computed and tested but never displayed; the page tests are regex over the HTML source and never execute the inline script.
Weights and verdict cutoffs are unsourced heuristics presented as a precise percentage.

verdict: A small, honest, correct screening tool: the Section 3509, FUTA and FLSA arithmetic reproduced exactly against an independent recomputation on three scenarios, the privacy and disclaimer claims are backed by files, and the page does what the README says. It does not meet the bar because verification scores 2: of four seeded mutations in calc.mjs, the two on the classification thresholds (the product's headline output) survived all tests. Domain and fitness are held at 2 by the single undifferentiated ABC result with no state context, unsourced weights presented as percentages, and unstated assumptions in the exposure number (non-exempt overtime, FUTA credit, no withholding in the high case). Cheap fixes: boundary tests for the 0.6, 0.35 and 0.5 cutoffs, a one-line note that the ABC result applies only in states using it, absolute URLs in canonical, sitemap, robots and llms.txt.
